hook.text: James Howells accidentally threw away a hard drive with 7,500 Bitcoin. Worth $500 million. It's still in a landfill.

buildup.text: A crypto wallet doesn't store coins. It stores private keys—the passwords that prove you own coins on the blockchain.

discovery.text: Public key: your address, like an email. Private key: your password. Share the first. Never share the second.

twist.text: About 20% of all Bitcoin is permanently lost—roughly $100 billion in coins whose owners lost their keys.

climax.text: Not your keys, not your coins. If an exchange holds your crypto, they control it. You trust them.

punchline.text: Your keys, your coins. Lose the keys, lose everything.

quiz.question: What does a crypto wallet actually store?
